overview.audience: Business users, new IT staff, and anyone who needs foundational Azure and cloud vocabulary.
overview.format_notes: The live exam is scored on a scale of up to 1000; ~700 is a common passing bar. This app uses 45 questions and a 70% practice threshold to mimic timing and breadth, not exact exam items.

sections.heading: What is cloud computing?
paragraphs: Cloud computing delivers compute, storage, networking, and applications over the internet with on-demand provisioning and pay-for-use pricing.
Key characteristics include broad network access, resource pooling, rapid elasticity, and measured service.

sections.heading: Cloud service models
bullets: IaaS — You manage OS, middleware, runtime, data, and apps; provider manages physical infrastructure and virtualization.
PaaS — You manage applications and data; provider manages runtime, middleware, OS, and infrastructure.
SaaS — You consume software over the internet; provider manages nearly the entire stack.

sections.heading: Deployment models
bullets: Public cloud — Shared provider infrastructure (e.g., Azure regions).
Private cloud — Dedicated to one organization; may be on-premises or hosted.
Hybrid cloud — Connects public and private with orchestration for migration and burst scenarios.

sections.heading: Economics and benefits
bullets: CapEx vs OpEx — Cloud shifts many costs from upfront capital to operational spend.
Elasticity and scalability — Scale out/in to match demand instead of over-provisioning hardware.
High availability and fault tolerance — Design for redundancy across zones and regions.
Consumption-based pricing — Meters usage; reservations and savings plans reduce cost for steady workloads.

sections.heading: Shared responsibility
paragraphs: Security and management duties depend on the service model. The provider always secures the physical datacenter and platform; the customer always owns data, identities, and access control choices.
SaaS shifts more responsibility to the provider; IaaS leaves more OS and network configuration to the customer.

sections.heading: Core architecture
bullets: Regions and region pairs — Geographic areas for deployment; pairs support disaster recovery within a geography.
Availability Zones — Physically separate datacenters within a region for resiliency.
Resource groups — Logical containers for resources that share lifecycle.
Subscriptions — Billing and access boundary; organized under management groups.
Azure Resource Manager (ARM) — Deployment and management layer; templates enable infrastructure as code.

sections.heading: Compute
bullets: Virtual Machines — Full control of the guest OS (IaaS).
Virtual Machine Scale Sets — Identical VMs with autoscale.
Azure App Service — Managed web and API hosting (PaaS).
Azure Functions — Event-driven, serverless code.
Azure Container Instances / AKS — Containers without or with Kubernetes orchestration.
Azure Virtual Desktop — Desktop and app virtualization.

sections.heading: Networking
bullets: Virtual Network (VNet) — Private network isolation in Azure.
VPN Gateway and ExpressRoute — Hybrid connectivity (internet VPN vs private circuit).
Azure DNS — Host DNS domains and records.
Load Balancer and Application Gateway — Layer 4 vs Layer 7 traffic distribution; App Gateway can include WAF.
Network Security Groups — Allow/deny traffic by IP, port, and protocol.

sections.heading: Storage
bullets: Blob storage — Unstructured object data; tiers Hot, Cool, and Archive.
Azure Files — SMB/NFS file shares.
Disk Storage — Block storage for VMs.
Table and Queue storage — NoSQL key-value and asynchronous messaging.
Redundancy — LRS, ZRS, GRS, and geo-zone options trade cost vs durability.

sections.heading: Data and analytics (fundamentals level)
bullets: Azure SQL Database — Managed relational PaaS.
Azure Cosmos DB — Global, multi-model NoSQL with configurable consistency.
Synapse Analytics — Enterprise analytics and data warehousing at a high level.

sections.heading: Identity and security services
bullets: Microsoft Entra ID — Identity, SSO, and access for cloud applications.
RBAC — Grant actions on scopes via built-in and custom roles.
Conditional Access and MFA — Risk-based policies and multi-step sign-in.
Microsoft Defender for Cloud — Secure score and workload protection recommendations.
Key Vault — Central store for secrets, keys, and certificates.
Azure Firewall, DDoS Protection, and Bastion — Network protection and secure admin access to VMs.

sections.heading: Management tools
bullets: Azure Portal — Web UI for resources.
Azure Cloud Shell — Browser shell with Bash/PowerShell and CLI.
Azure CLI and Azure PowerShell — Cross-platform and scriptable administration.
ARM templates and Bicep — Repeatable, declarative deployments.
Azure Arc — Extend Azure management to hybrid and multicloud resources.

sections.heading: Governance and compliance
bullets: Management groups — Hierarchy above subscriptions for policy and RBAC inheritance.
Azure Policy — Enforce organizational standards (allow/deny/remediate).
Resource locks — CanNotDelete or ReadOnly protection.
Tags — Metadata for cost allocation and automation.
Microsoft Purview — Data governance and catalog (awareness level).
Service Trust Portal — Compliance documentation and audit reports.

sections.heading: Monitoring and reliability
bullets: Azure Monitor — Metrics, logs, alerts, and dashboards.
Log Analytics — Query and analyze log data (KQL).
Azure Service Health — Platform incidents and planned maintenance.
Azure Advisor — Free recommendations for cost, security, reliability, performance, and operations.
Well-Architected Framework — Five pillars: reliability, security, cost optimization, operational excellence, performance efficiency.

sections.heading: Cost management
bullets: Azure pricing calculator — Estimate spend before deployment.
Cost Management + Billing — Budgets, alerts, and analysis.
TCO calculator — Compare on-premises vs Azure costs.
Cost optimization — Right-size resources, reservations, and eliminating waste.
